title: Diagonal nerve detects weak equivalences between cofibrant homotopy groupoids
statement: Fix a small set $O$. Use the fixed-object model structure on simplicial categories on $O$ and functors fixing $O$ from [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], for the $O\times O$-sorted algebraic theory of associative composition and identities. Weak equivalences and fibrations are weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations on each mapping simplicial set. Cofibrant means that the map from the identity-only category on $O$ has the left lifting property against every mappingwise trivial Kan fibration. Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $u:U\to V$ be an object-preserving simplicial functor between cofibrant objects in this model structure. Suppose that both ordinary path-component categories $\pi_0U$ and $\pi_0V$ are groupoids; their morphisms are path components of the mapping simplicial sets. For a simplicial category $T$ on $O$, put $B(T)_{p,q}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p\in O}\prod_{r=1}^p T(x_{r-1},x_r)_q$; the first-direction operators compose or omit arrows and insert identities, and the second-direction operators are those of the mapping sets. Empty products are singletons. Its diagonal classifying nerve is $NT=\operatorname{diag}B(T)$. Then $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on every mapping simplicial set if and only if $Nu:NU\to NV$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets. No Kan, connectedness, or nonemptiness assumption is imposed on the mapping sets or on $O$.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Corollary 9.6, printed p.280; the diagonal nerve is 1.4(vi), and the fixed-object model is 7.2. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy theorem.

proof.text: First note that any object-preserving mappingwise weak equivalence $g:A\to D$ induces a weak equivalence $Ng$. At each fixed nerve degree $p$, $B(g)_{p,\bullet}$ is a coproduct, indexed by the same strings of objects, of finite products of mappingwise weak equivalences. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], realization preserves those products and coproducts. Paths and based cubical maps into a finite product are tuples, as are their homotopies, so components and based homotopy groups are products of the corresponding components and groups of the factors. A path or based cube in a disjoint union stays in its chosen summand. Consequently the row maps are weak equivalences. Empty products, empty factors, and an empty indexing set satisfy the same assertion. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to get $Ng$ a weak equivalence. In particular this proves the forward implication for $u$.

source.place: 1.4(vi)-(vii), pp.269; forward implication of Corollary 9.6, p.280.

proof.text: For the converse suppose $Nu$ is a weak equivalence. Apply $R=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ to each mapping simplicial set and use its canonical finite-product comparisons to define composition and identities. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], this gives locally Kan simplicial categories $C=RU$, $D=RV$, a functor $f=Ru:C\to D$, and natural mappingwise weak equivalences $U\to C$, $V\to D$. Associativity and units hold because the comparisons commute with product projections. The units induce bijections of mapping components preserving composition, so $\pi_0C$ and $\pi_0D$ are groupoids. By step 1, $NU\to NC$ and $NV\to ND$ are weak equivalences. Their naturality square with $Nu,Nf$ commutes on every string of arrows, hence two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] gives $Nf$ a weak equivalence. Cofibrancy of the replacements is unnecessary.

source.place: Corollary 9.6 and Proposition 9.5, p.280; explicit functorial mappingwise Kan replacement before the bar argument.

proof.text: For $T=C$ or $D$ and a vertex $a\in T(s,t)_0$, choose $b\in T(t,s)_0$ in its inverse component. Such a vertex exists: every point of a realized simplex is joined to a vertex, so every component has a vertex representative. The composites $ba,ab$ are joined to the identities by paths in the realized endomorphism sets. Composition and these paths, using the product comparison in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], give homotopies from the two composites of $a^*:|T(t,y)|\to|T(s,y)|$ and $b^*$ to the identity maps. Thus precomposition by $a$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. This holds for each $y$ and for any finite composite of arrows, including an identity. If either mapping set is empty, the existence of both precomposition maps forces the other to be empty as well.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 proof, p.280: the groupoidal-component hypothesis makes the bar action maps equivalences.

proof.text:
Fix $y\in O$. For $T=C,D$ form
$$E(T,y)_{p,q}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p\in O}\left(\prod_{i=1}^pT(x_{i-1},x_i)_q\right)\times T(x_p,y)_q.$$
The nerve operators drop the first arrow, compose adjacent arrows, or compose the last arrow with the final entry; degeneracies insert identities. The other direction acts on the mapping sets. Associativity, units and simplicial composition verify the identities and commutation of the directions. Forget the final entry to obtain $p_T:E(T,y)\to B(T)$. At each nerve degree this is a map of Kan complexes and is a Kan fibration: each summand is a projection from a product with the Kan complex $T(x_p,y)$. Horn lifts are constructed coordinatewise in the summand selected by the horn. Horns are nonempty and connected, including the single-vertex horns in dimension one, so empty fibers cause no lifting problem. At nerve degree zero, the strict fiber over $x\in O$ is precisely $T(x,y)$. Applying $f$ to every entry gives a commuting square of the two bar projections.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 proof, p.280: N(V,V), restricted to the component with last target y; bisimplicial formula and projection.

proof.text:
For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ compare the naturality square of $p_T$ with
$$P=B(T)_{n,\bullet}\times_{B(T)_{m,\bullet}}E(T,y)_{m,\bullet}.$$
Put $A=B(T)_{n,\bullet}$. The projections $E(T,y)_{n,\bullet}\to A$ and $P\to A$ are Kan fibrations between Kan complexes: pullback horn fillers are obtained by projecting the horn and lifting through $p_{T,m}$. Over a vertex $(x_0\xrightarrow{a_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_n}x_n)$ the comparison on strict fibers is
$$T(x_n,y)\longrightarrow T(x_{\alpha(m)},y),\qquad h\longmapsto h\,a_n\cdots a_{\alpha(m)+1}.$$
It is a weak equivalence by step 3. Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to each projection and the map $\Delta^0\to A$ selecting this vertex. It identifies each strict fiber with its path-model homotopy fiber by a weak equivalence. These comparisons commute with the map $E_n\to P$: both insert the constant path at the common basepoint. Thus the homotopy-fiber map is a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with base map $1_A$ and constant commutation homotopy to deduce that $E_n\to P$ is a weak equivalence. Finally the strict pullback P computes the homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], since its three entries are Kan and the leg $E_m\to B_m$ is a Kan fibration. All naturality squares are therefore homotopy pullbacks.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 proof, p.280: verify the homotopy-cartesian bar squares explicitly instead of invoking an unspecified quasifibration theorem.

proof.text:
The diagrams in step 4 are small, levelwise Kan, and their projections are levelwise Kan fibrations. Step 5 checks every naturality square, including those for arbitrary monotone maps. Therefore [lem-coef-equifibered-bisimplicial-diagonal] gives a weak equivalence
$$T(x,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_x\bigl(\operatorname{diag}E(T,y)\longrightarrow NT\bigr).$$
Its naturality in $p_T$ identifies the induced map of fibers for $C,D$ with $f_{x,y}$, since $f$ fixes $O$ and acts on every entry of the two bars. Homotopy fibers of the possibly non-Kan diagonals are computed after functorial Kan replacement, exactly as required in the cited statement.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 proof, p.280: bar-fiber comparison; Corollary 9.6 uses its naturality for U to V.

proof.text: For fixed $q$, the simplicial set $E(T,y)_{\bullet,q}$ is the ordinary nerve of $T_q/y$. Indeed a chain in this slice is uniquely a chain $x_0\to\cdots\to x_p$ with a last map $x_p\to y$; all other arrows to $y$ are its successive composites. The slice has terminal object $1_y$. Its unique arrows to $1_y$ form a natural transformation from the identity functor to the constant functor. Apply [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] to the functors to and from the terminal category; their composites have the required natural transformations, so $E(T,y)_{\bullet,q}\to *$ is a weak equivalence. The exchanged-direction assertion of [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] gives $\operatorname{diag}E(T,y)\to *$ a weak equivalence. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] now shows that the bar map for $f$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 9.5 proof, p.280: contractibility of each fixed-target component of N(V,V), expanded via its terminal slices.

proof.text:
The square of diagonal bar projections has a weak equivalence on total spaces by step 7 and on bases by step 2. Apply functorial Kan replacement to that square. Naturality of the unit and two-out-of-three preserve both weak equivalences. The point selecting $x$ is preserved because $f$ fixes $O$. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to the two cospans consisting of the replaced bar projection and this point: it gives a weak equivalence of homotopy fibers. Together with the natural comparisons in step 6 this proves $f_{x,y}$ a weak equivalence by two-out-of-three. Finally
$$f_{x,y}\eta_{U(x,y)}=\eta_{V(x,y)}u_{x,y}.$$
Both units are weak equivalences by [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], so two-out-of-three proves $u_{x,y}$ a weak equivalence. This works for every pair $x,y$, allowing empty fibers. If $O$ is empty both nerves are empty and there are no mapping assertions to check. No connectedness reduction or initial Kan assumption has been used.

source.place: Corollary 9.6, p.280, using the natural bar-fiber argument of Proposition 9.5; explicit comparison and removal of Kan replacement.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 9.6 and the bar argument of Proposition 9.5, p.280; online source read, archival copy unavailable; explicit replacement and homotopy-fiber proof using existing DAG lemmas.

lean.statement: theorem groupoidal_cofibrant_nerve_detection {O : Type u} {U V : Fixed O} (f : U ⟶ V) (hU : fixedCofibrations O (discreteInclusion U)) (hV : fixedCofibrations O (discreteInclusion V)) (hgroupU : ∀ (a b : O) (e : (U.Hom a b) _⦋0⦌), IsEquivalenceVertex U e) (hgroupV : ∀ (a b : O) (e : (V.Hom a b) _⦋0⦌), IsEquivalenceVertex V e) : fixedWeakEquivalences O f ↔ Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (CategoryTheory.TwoSidedSimplicialGrothendieck.diagonalNerveMap (degreeDiagramMap f))
